ghi_chu.ly_do: Sash windows were only just appearing in London in the 1670s and 1680s. They were not common on ordinary street houses until the early 18th century.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The man walking in the foreground wears a tall, straight-sided, narrow-brimmed black top hat. His coat is a plain, long, dark frock-style coat.
ghi_chu.ly_do: This hat shape is a late 18th to 19th century top hat. Around 1680 men wore broad-brimmed, lower-crowned or sugar-loaf hats, and fashionable men wore periwigs.

tra_loi.vat: Tall black crowned hat worn by a man walking in the street (headgear)
tra_loi.dac_diem: The hat is dark and tall with a flat top, a slightly tapered crown and a narrow brim. It looks like a plain, buckle-less sugarloaf or capotain hat. The man also wears a long dark coat with a belt and dark boots. The image is blurry, so I can't make out a hat band or buckle.
tra_loi.ly_do: Tall-crowned black hats (capotain/sugarloaf style) were worn in England from about the late 16th century, and Puritan-style plain versions were still common around 1680. Nothing visible, such as a top-hat silhouette or a buckle, points to a later design.
